reviewMethod: Read the fixed REC statements and surrounding paragraphs/lists/terms for R3's bounded definition omissions. Distinguish AND/OR, inherited HTML/SVG scope, conditional scheme case sensitivity, lowercase advice, and MIME transfer encoding from ZIP compression. This is not full REC independent reading, product execution, or S0 approval.

constraints.reason: Parent same-group follow-up: HTML script data blocks are exempt from fallback requirements. Read p1/p2 explaining why intrinsic/manifest fallbacks do not apply; this does not exempt executable script resources or other foreign content.
constraints.applicability: Inline HTML script data blocks only; distinguish executable scripted content and standalone resources.
constraints.phase: T2 fallback/content classification; T4b XHTML preservation

constraints.reason: Parent same-group follow-up: lowercase should recommends a single title for consistent rendering. It is not a MUST or a prohibition on multiple titles; p2's main-title ordering still applies.
constraints.applicability: EPUB creator title metadata advice, not a requirement for a new reading UI.
constraints.phase: T2 metadata model; T4a metadata authoring

constraints.reason: Parent same-group follow-up: lowercase should recommends the creator name intended for display, distinct from optional normalized file-as and alternate-script values. No BCP14 MUST or executed presentation is inferred.
constraints.applicability: Creator display-name metadata advice.
constraints.phase: T2 metadata model; T4a metadata authoring; S2-S4 presentation

constraints.reason: Parent same-group follow-up: when there is more than one creator, lowercase should recommends separate dc:creator elements. This is not a BCP14 MUST; ordering and primary-creator semantics remain separate.
constraints.applicability: Multiple-creator metadata authoring.
constraints.phase: T2 metadata model; T4a metadata authoring

constraints.reason: Parent same-group follow-up: lowercase should recommends dc:contributor for secondary contributors, not an obligatory role vocabulary or prohibition on optional refinements.
constraints.applicability: Secondary-contributor metadata advice.
constraints.phase: T2 metadata model; T4a metadata authoring

constraints.reason: Parent same-group follow-up: each meta defines an expression whose property value defines the statement and whose text represents the assertion. This relation is distinct from primary/refined expression classification.
constraints.applicability: Package meta property/text semantics.
constraints.phase: T2 metadata graph; T4a metadata maintenance

constraints.reason: Parent same-group follow-up: Meta Properties Vocabulary is the default for meta property. This does not supply a default for scheme or authorize declaring a default prefix.
constraints.applicability: Package meta property values, not all property datatype attributes.
constraints.phase: T2 vocabulary resolution; T4a metadata maintenance

constraints.reason: Parent same-group follow-up: Metadata Link Vocabulary is the default for link rel and properties. Preserve the attribute/element scope; other vocabularies remain separately permitted under prefix mechanisms.
constraints.applicability: Package link rel/properties values only.
constraints.phase: T2 vocabulary resolution; T4a metadata maintenance

constraints.reason: Parent same-group follow-up: Manifest Properties Vocabulary is the default for item properties, distinct from Meta, Link and Spine vocabularies and from the conditional property-declaration list.
constraints.applicability: Manifest item properties values only.
constraints.phase: T2 vocabulary/resource classification; T4a package maintenance

constraints.reason: Parent same-group follow-up: Spine Properties Vocabulary is the default for itemref properties, not for manifest item properties or meta property. Existing scheme/default-prefix rules are not duplicated.
constraints.applicability: Spine itemref properties values only.
constraints.phase: T2 vocabulary/spine model; T4a package maintenance

constraints.reason: General exemption definition introduces two necessary conditions joined by AND, in addition to separately registered content-specific exemptions; the introductory paragraph alone cannot replace either leaf.
constraints.applicability: Classifying a container resource under the general exemption: neither spine-itemref reference nor direct content-document embedding.
constraints.phase: T2 resource/fallback classification; T3 migration; S2 resources

constraints.reason: Each leaf is a necessary member of the general exemption's AND: no spine itemref reference AND no direct embedding in an EPUB content document. Neither leaf alone grants exemption; existing content-specific exemptions are distinct.
constraints.applicability: General exempt-resource classification, not a blanket exemption for all unrendered or foreign resources.
constraints.phase: T2 resource/fallback classification; T3 migration; S2 resources

constraints.reason: SVG embedded by reference remains an SVG core media type governed by the SVG content-document requirements. The img/object examples illustrate referencing and are not required embedding mechanisms.
constraints.applicability: SVG referenced by an XHTML content document; distinguish reference from inline inclusion.
constraints.phase: T2 resource/content profiles; T4b XHTML editing; S2-S4 rendering

constraints.reason: SVG included as a document fragment in XHTML inherits the same content conformance restrictions as SVG content documents in sec-svg-restrictions. This includes the 2026 restriction scope; inline markup is not exempt.
constraints.applicability: SVG directly included in XHTML, not just standalone SVG resources; no requirement to implement rendering at S0.
constraints.phase: T2 content profiles; T4b XHTML editing; S2-S4 rendering

constraints.reason: The restriction-list introduction binds both SVG content documents and SVG embedded by inclusion in XHTML. Existing restriction leaves keep their levels; this scope sentence does not replace them.
constraints.applicability: Both standalone SVG content documents and SVG included in XHTML, subject to each leaf's own conditions.
constraints.phase: T2 content profiles; T4b XHTML editing; S2-S4 rendering

constraints.reason: A package link target is a publication resource only under either following condition. The OR differs from the general exempt-resource AND and does not make every linked metadata record a publication resource.
constraints.applicability: Package-document link targets; otherwise the following p4's existing manifest prohibition remains applicable.
constraints.phase: T2 link/resource model; T3 migration; T4a metadata

constraints.reason: Each leaf is an alternative: referenced from the spine OR included/embedded in an EPUB content document. Either can establish publication-resource status; they are not simultaneous requirements and the RDFa/JSON-LD examples are not mandatory formats.
constraints.applicability: Determining whether a package link target is a publication resource, distinct from standalone linked metadata.
constraints.phase: T2 link/resource model; T3 migration; T4a metadata

constraints.reason: Dublin Core elements and meta have mandatory child text content, called their value. Existing p2's nonempty-after-ASCII-trim MUST is separate; data presence is not inferred from an attribute.
constraints.applicability: Package metadata Dublin Core and meta values, not every XML element.
constraints.phase: T2 metadata parsing/preservation; T4a metadata maintenance

constraints.reason: Whitespace within metadata values is insignificant and runs collapse to a single space during processing. This is distinct from p2's leading/trailing ASCII stripping and does not authorize rewriting preserved source bytes.
constraints.applicability: Processing Dublin Core/meta value semantics; raw preservation and parsed value are distinct.
constraints.phase: T2 metadata model; T4a metadata maintenance

constraints.reason: The first dc:title in document order is the main title. Other title occurrences are not forbidden; neighboring lowercase single-title advice is not upgraded into MUST.
constraints.applicability: Package dc:title ordering, including multiple-title publications.
constraints.phase: T2 metadata model; T3 migration; T4a metadata; S2-S4 presentation

constraints.reason: Document order sets creator display priority and the first dc:creator is primary. This does not require a new display implementation or constrain author names to a particular role vocabulary.
constraints.applicability: Package creator metadata order; distinguish creator/contributor and optional role refinements.
constraints.phase: T2 metadata model; T3 migration; T4a metadata; S2-S4 presentation

constraints.reason: An HTML script element holding a data block does not represent scripted content. Do not infer executable scripting merely from the presence of script markup; surrounding active-script/form classification remains separate.
constraints.applicability: Classifying HTML script data blocks, not granting execution or arbitrary data-block support.
constraints.phase: T2 content/resource classification; T4b XHTML preservation; S2-S4 script policy

constraints.reason: The two script execution contexts introduce the separately registered container-constrained and spine-level definitions; this is classification, not a mandate to execute both.
constraints.applicability: Context classification when scripted content is encountered.
constraints.phase: T2 content profiles; T4b XHTML preservation; S2-S4 script policy

constraints.reason: The two distinct context definitions bind iframe-contained execution versus direct top-level execution. Each context is recorded independently; optional reading-system support is not promoted to an S0 execution requirement.
constraints.applicability: Classifying actual script context; container-constrained and spine-level support retain their own conditions.
constraints.phase: T2 content profiles; T4b XHTML preservation; S2-S4 script policy

constraints.reason: Inline script code and code referenced through src have the same context classification. Transport/location of the code does not switch an iframe script into spine-level context.
constraints.applicability: Context classification for direct and src-referenced code, not permission for network execution.
constraints.phase: T2 content profiles; T4b XHTML preservation; S2-S4 script policy

constraints.reason: A container-constrained script is either of the following HTML/SVG cases, both requiring the stated iframe embedding context. The alternatives are not cumulative requirements.
constraints.applicability: Identifying container-constrained scripts; no new scripting feature or permission to modify the embedding document.
constraints.phase: T2 content profiles; T4b XHTML preservation; S2-S4 script policy

constraints.reason: HTML script in iframe-embedded XHTML OR SVG script in iframe-embedded SVG qualifies as container constrained. Both refer to embedding in XHTML; preserve the distinction and the parent's either operator.
constraints.applicability: HTML/SVG container-constrained script classification; existing embedding-DOM/rectangle MUST NOT rules remain unchanged.
constraints.phase: T2 content profiles; T4b XHTML preservation; S2-S4 script policy

constraints.reason: A spine-level script is an HTML or SVG script in a top-level content document. The subsequent conditional support advice and progressive-enhancement SHOULD are not replaced by this definition.
constraints.applicability: Top-level document script classification, not all RS scripting implementation at S0.
constraints.phase: T2 content profiles; T4b XHTML preservation; S2-S4 script policy

constraints.reason: A primary metadata expression establishes an aspect of the publication; omitting refines defines a primary expression. Do not treat omitted refines as an unresolved secondary target.
constraints.applicability: Package meta expressions without refines.
constraints.phase: T2 metadata graph; T3 migration; T4a metadata maintenance

constraints.reason: A subexpression uses refines to associate with another expression or resource and enhance its meaning. Duration/creator examples illustrate refinements; they are not mandatory metadata properties.
constraints.applicability: Package meta expressions with refines; existing chaining permission and target constraints remain separate.
constraints.phase: T2 metadata graph; T3 migration; T4a metadata maintenance

constraints.reason: linear=yes contributes sequential primary reading order, while no identifies auxiliary content accessible out of sequence. Auxiliary examples are not an exhaustive list; existing omitted-linear=yes and at-least-one-linear MUST remain unchanged.
constraints.applicability: Spine itemref linear semantics, not a requirement to provide a new reading UI.
constraints.phase: T2 spine model; T3 migration; T4a maintenance; S2-S4 reading order

constraints.reason: Non-linear is a purpose hint and does not prescribe presentation. Reading systems may present it in spine order or later; do not turn examples into a mandatory popup or skipping behavior.
constraints.applicability: Reading-system handling of non-linear spine content; required access mechanism is a separately registered MUST.
constraints.phase: T2 spine preservation; S2-S4 optional presentation

constraints.reason: Subject and term values are case sensitive only when the designated scheme requires it. Do not impose universal case sensitivity or mandate case folding when a scheme does not require sensitivity.
constraints.applicability: Subject metadata with scheme-dependent case semantics; existing scheme/term association constraints remain separate.
constraints.phase: T2 metadata comparison; T3 migration; T4a metadata maintenance

constraints.reason: Unless otherwise specified, normative XHTML requirements inherit HTML semantics, structure and processing. The similar sec-overview-relations-html p3 is inside an informative overview and is not promoted; EPUB-specific deviations remain effective.
constraints.applicability: XHTML content documents under actual normative sec-xhtml-req, subject to explicit EPUB overrides.
constraints.phase: T1 syntax profiles; T2 content model; T4b XHTML editing; S2-S4 rendering

constraints.reason: OCF paths and filenames are Unicode scalar value strings and their values are case sensitive. This is not the same as the separate canonical-normalization/full-case-fold uniqueness rule for names in a directory.
constraints.applicability: OCF abstract-container path/name identities, not OS-specific case normalization.
constraints.phase: T1 path/resource identity; T2 references; T6 packaging

constraints.reason: A content URL results from parsing the file path with the container-root URL as base. Preserve file/directory scope; it is not raw string concatenation or an authorization to fetch external content.
constraints.applicability: OCF file/directory content-URL derivation.
constraints.phase: T1 resource identities; T2 URL/reference model; S2 resource service

constraints.reason: Valid relative OCF URL with fragment first requires a path-relative-scheme-less URL, optionally followed by # and a URL fragment, AND the formal steps must return true. Registered algorithm leaves alone do not express these syntax prerequisites.
constraints.applicability: Relative OCF URL validity, distinct from absolute URL permission in the subsequent requirement.
constraints.phase: T1 resource identities; T2 URL/reference validation; S2 resources

constraints.reason: Omitting a prefix resolves the reference in that attribute's default vocabulary. Do not assume one global default vocabulary for all attributes or invent a default for scheme.
constraints.applicability: Unprefixed property values in attributes with the defined default vocabulary.
constraints.phase: T2 metadata/property semantics; T4a authoring; S2-S4 vocabulary handling

constraints.reason: prefix is not namespaced in the package document, unlike the separately specified OPS namespace in content/media-overlay documents. Keep these document profiles distinct.
constraints.applicability: Package-document prefix attribute only; not a blanket prohibition on epub:prefix elsewhere.
constraints.phase: T1 XML profiles; T2 property association; T4a metadata authoring

constraints.reason: For multiple roles attached to one person/organization, lowercase should recommends descending importance in meta document order. It is not a marked BCP14 MUST and does not forbid multiple roles.
constraints.applicability: Multiple role metadata refinements; distinguish from the preceding marked scheme SHOULD.
constraints.phase: T2 metadata order; T4a metadata authoring; S2-S4 presentation

constraints.reason: Package media registration distinguishes UTF-8 8bit compatibility from UTF-16 binary transfer encoding. These are MIME encoding considerations, not ZIP compression methods.
constraints.applicability: application/oebps-package+xml media-type handling and transfer encoding; XML bytes remain UTF-8 or UTF-16.
constraints.phase: T1 XML decoding; T2 media profiles; T6 packaging; S2 resource response

constraints.reason: UTF-16 package documents require binary content-transfer-encoding; UTF-8 is 8bit compatible. Preserve the conditional lowercase must in media registration without inventing a ZIP STORE/DEFLATE rule.
constraints.applicability: MIME transfer of package documents, conditional on UTF-16; not a blanket requirement to transcode preserved OPF.
constraints.phase: T1 XML decoding; T2 media profiles; T6 packaging; S2 resource response

constraints.reason: Package documents contain well-formed XML conforming to XML 1.0. Record this media-registration format definition without treating following attack examples as additional normative algorithms.
constraints.applicability: application/oebps-package+xml processors; existing package/OCF XML restrictions remain distinct.
constraints.phase: T1 XML import; T2 resource validation

constraints.reason: Lowercase should advises package processors to rigorously check retrieved data size and validity. It is not BCP14 MUST; product budgets remain product policy rather than invented standard constants.
constraints.applicability: Processors reading package documents, including actual acquisition/processing boundaries.
constraints.phase: T1 resource budgets/XML import; T2 validation; S2 resources

constraints.reason: OCF containers are binary files encoded in application/zip. This media-registration statement is distinct from the package XML MIME transfer-encoding rule and from specific ZIP-entry compression constraints.
constraints.applicability: application/epub+zip container format handling.
constraints.phase: T1 ZIP import; T6 packaging; S2 resource response

constraints.reason: Lowercase should advises OCF ZIP processors to rigorously check data size and validity. No standard numeric budget or universally supported behavior is inferred.
constraints.applicability: Processors reading OCF ZIP container files; additional embedded formats have their own processing/security scope.
constraints.phase: T1 ZIP/resource budgets; T2 validation; S2 resources

constraints.reason: application/zip security considerations also apply to OCF containers. Additional embedded formats can add security considerations when processed; this does not imply all such formats execute at S0.
constraints.applicability: OCF ZIP container processing, with actual downstream processing boundaries.
constraints.phase: T1 ZIP import/security; T2 validation; T6 packaging; S2 resources

sectionNotes.sec-exempt-resources: R3 correction: read p4 and ul1 with the preceding content-specific dl and following examples. General exemption is no spine reference AND no direct embedding; content-specific cases remain separate. Added p4 and both independent leaves. Examples/format-support discussion are not universal obligations. This bounded source review is not independent full-REC acceptance or execution.
sectionNotes.sec-xhtml-svg: R3 correction: read p1 and both embedding definitions. Reference invokes SVG core media-type requirements; inclusion inherits sec-svg-restrictions. The img/object examples do not require particular embedding mechanisms. Both definitions now have independent source rows; no new renderer or RS execution claimed.
sectionNotes.sec-svg-restrictions: R3 correction: read p1, restriction leaves and intervening notes. The introduction explicitly applies existing restriction leaves to both SVG documents and SVG included in XHTML; marked leaf levels remain unchanged. The note excluding HTML body for included SVG is context, not a new BCP14 obligation. This is scope registration, not whole SVG/HTML implementation evidence.
sectionNotes.sec-link-elem: R3 correction: read p2-p6 and p8-p11 with p3/ul1. A target becomes a publication resource when spine-referenced OR content-included/embedded; otherwise existing p4 manifest MUST NOT remains. p10 supplies Metadata Link Vocabulary specifically for rel/properties. Two alternative conditions are not an AND or a mandate to retrieve external metadata.
sectionNotes.sec-metadata-values: R3 correction: read all three paragraphs. p1 mandatory child text and p3 internal whitespace collapse now have rows; existing p2 nonempty-after-ASCII-strip MUST remains. Semantic processing is not authority to normalize preserved source bytes or proof of passed metadata behavior.
sectionNotes.sec-opf-dctitle: R3 correction: read title definition, usage, p2 order and p3 single-title advice. The first title is main, not the only allowed title. Registered p2 and lowercase should in p3 separately; the latter is advisory, not BCP14 MUST. No new title UI or executed support claimed.
sectionNotes.sec-opf-dccreator: R3 correction: read all six creator paragraphs and examples. p5 document order determines display priority/primary creator; role/file-as/alternate-script mechanisms remain optional. Separately register lowercase should in p2 (intended display name), conditional p4 (separate creators), and p6 (secondary contributors). None is promoted to MUST or executed display support.
sectionNotes.sec-scripted-support: R3 correction: read p1-p5. HTML script data blocks are not scripted content (p3); active scripting/forms and scripted manifest property remain separately classified. This records a source distinction, not new script execution or a permission to share publication origins.
sectionNotes.sec-scripted-context: R3 correction: read p1/ul1/p2 and child context sections. iframe-contained versus top-level execution defines the two contexts; inline code versus src makes no difference to context. Intro, two definitions and location-invariance now have rows. This is not an obligation to implement both script contexts.
sectionNotes.sec-scripted-container-constrained: R3 correction: read p1/ul1 and p2-p4 restrictions/advice. Either HTML script in iframe-embedded XHTML OR SVG script in iframe-embedded SVG qualifies. Existing DOM/rectangle MUST NOT records remain; recommended/optional support boundaries do not become new CLI execution requirements.
sectionNotes.sec-scripted-spine: R3 correction: read p1-p3. HTML/SVG script in a top-level document defines spine-level context; later conditional support advice and progressive-enhancement SHOULD remain separate. Added only missing p1, without runtime execution claims.
sectionNotes.sec-meta-elem: R3 correction: read p2/p3/ul1 and p4-p7 refines/scheme/default discussion. p2 binds property to statement and text to assertion; omitting refines yields a primary expression, while refines associates a subexpression. p5 supplies Meta vocabulary specifically for property, whereas scheme has no default. Examples do not mandate duration/author metadata; existing chaining and prefix rules stay unchanged.
sectionNotes.sec-itemref-elem: R3 correction: read p4-p10. yes contributes primary sequential reading; no denotes auxiliary content without prescribed presentation. Existing omitted-linear=yes, at-least-one-linear MUST and access MUST retain identities. p4/p6 independently preserve meaning/permission; p9 supplies Spine vocabulary for itemref properties, not manifest properties. No reading UI added.
sectionNotes.html-script-element: Parent same-group R3 follow-up: read all three paragraphs. p1 explains unavailable intrinsic/manifest fallbacks and p2 the absence of user-rendered raw data. p3 explicitly exempts inline script data blocks from fallback requirements. Record the exemption, not the explanation as extra obligations; executable scripts and standalone foreign resources are not generally exempt.
sectionNotes.sec-item-resource-properties: Parent same-group R3 follow-up: read p1-p7 and existing conditional property list. p2 supplies Manifest vocabulary for item properties; p3/list conditional declarations and p4 nonrecursive scope remain separate. Do not apply Meta/Link/Spine defaults here or require every item to carry every property. No executed vocabulary support claimed.
sectionNotes.sec-opf-dcsubject: R3 correction: read p1-p5. Subject/term case sensitivity depends only on designated scheme requirements; it is not universal case sensitivity or mandatory case folding. Existing scheme/term MUST/MUST NOT retain their conditions; added p5 definition only.
sectionNotes.sec-xhtml-req: R3 correction: read requirements list and p2. Normative HTML inheritance applies unless explicitly overridden by EPUB. Added p2 from this normative section, not the near-duplicate informative sec-overview-relations-html p3. Existing marked content-model obligations remain; no whole HTML support declared.
sectionNotes.sec-overview-relations-html: R3 scope comparison: this entire overview inherits informative scope. Its p3 resembles sec-xhtml-req p2 but is not promoted to a normative row. The actual normative requirement is registered at sec-xhtml-req. Comparison of these two statements is bounded evidence, not full standards-body reading.
sectionNotes.sec-container-filenames: R3 correction: read p1/p2 and restriction list. Paths/names are scalar value strings and their values are case-sensitive. Directory-name uniqueness separately uses canonical normalization and full case folding; the new p1 definition does not replace that marked rule or OS/profile constraints.
sectionNotes.sec-container-iri: R3 correction: read p1-p5 and formal algorithm/Explanation distinction. p2 defines content URL by parsing path against container root; p3 requires path-relative-scheme-less syntax with optional fragment AND successful formal checks. Existing algorithm identities/branches remain; named Explanation stays non-normative and URL validity is not fetch authorization.
sectionNotes.sec-property-datatype: R3 correction: read datatype/grammar, two empty-value exclusions and p4. Unprefixed references resolve in that attribute's default vocabulary, not a global default for all attributes. Added p4; R2 empty-string and existing empty-reference rules retain identities. No executed vocabulary support claimed.
sectionNotes.sec-prefix-attr: R3 correction: read p1-p9 with namespace and reserved-prefix cases. Package prefix is unnamespaced (p4), unlike OPS namespace in content/media overlays; SVG inclusion has its own root-html rule. Added p4 without replacing existing marked declarations/prohibitions.
sectionNotes.sec-role: R3 correction: read role table description paragraphs and examples. For multiple roles, lowercase should recommends importance in meta document order. It is not a BCP14 MUST and is distinct from preceding scheme SHOULD. Added p3 only; multiple role values remain permitted.
sectionNotes.app-media-type-app-oebps-package: R3 correction: read registration Encoding/Security dt/dd pairs and surrounding paragraphs. Separate dd5 p1 compatibility and p2 conditional UTF-16 binary content-transfer-encoding; neither specifies ZIP compression. dd6 p1 defines XML well-formedness and p3 lowercase should advises size/validity checks. Attack discussion is context, not a new normative algorithm; numeric budgets are product policy.
sectionNotes.app-media-type: R3 correction: read registration Encoding/Security dt/dd pairs. dd5 p1 identifies binary application/zip; dd6 p1 lowercase should advises size/validity checks and p3 inherits ZIP security considerations. Additional embedded types have conditional downstream scope; this does not mandate executing all formats or make registration text a ZIP compression algorithm.
